content: Budesonide foam, commonly sold under the brand name Uceris, is a medication used to manage symptoms of ulcerative colitis, a type of bowel disease. It works by reducing inflammation and swelling in the affected areas. Budesonide belongs to a class of drugs known as corticosteroids. While it does not cure ulcerative colitis, it can help alleviate symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and bloody stools. How to Use: Before starting budesonide, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Follow the illustrated instructions for proper use. This medication is applied as a foam into the rectum, typically as directed by your doctor. For the first two weeks, it is usually applied in the morning and evening, followed by once-daily use in the evening for the next four weeks. To use the foam: 1. Warm the canister in your hands and shake it well for 10 to 15 seconds before use. 2. Attach the enclosed applicator to the canister as instructed. 3. Hold the canister upside down and gently insert the applicator tip into the anus. 4. Press down on the pump and hold it for 2 seconds to release the foam. 5. Keep the applicator in place for 10 to 15 seconds before removing it. 6. Dispose of the applicator after use and wash your hands thoroughly. It is best to use this medication after a bowel movement. Avoid inserting any part of the canister directly into the anus. This medication is flammable, so avoid smoking during and immediately after application. If you are transitioning from an oral corticosteroid (e.g., prednisone), do not stop taking it abruptly unless directed by your doctor. Sudden discontinuation may worsen certain conditions (e.g., asthma, allergies) or cause withdrawal symptoms such as weakness, weight loss, nausea, muscle pain, headache, tiredness, or dizziness. Your doctor may gradually reduce the dose of your previous medication while starting budesonide. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Take it at the same time(s) each day to help you remember. Do not increase the dose or use it more frequently than prescribed. Do not stop using this medication without consulting your doctor, as some conditions may worsen if the drug is stopped suddenly. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, headache, dizziness, abdominal pain, back pain, fatigue, and respiratory infections. Rarely, budesonide may be absorbed into the bloodstream, leading to systemic corticosteroid side effects, especially in children or those using the medication long-term. Budesonide may lower your ability to fight infections, increasing the risk of serious or even fatal infections. Notify your doctor if you experience symptoms of infection, such as fever or persistent sore throat. Rarely, a severe allergic reaction may occur. Precautions: Before using budesonide, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Long-term use of corticosteroids may make it harder for your body to respond to physical stress. Budesonide may also mask signs of infection or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections (e.g., chickenpox, measles, COVID-19). Inform your healthcare provider that you are using budesonide before receiving any vaccinations. Prolonged use in children may temporarily slow growth. During pregnancy, use this medication only when clearly needed, and discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Budesonide passes into breast milk, but it is not expected to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Budesonide may interact with other medications, altering their effects or increasing the risk of side effects. Inform your doctor of all medications and supplements you are taking. Avoid consuming grapefruit juice during treatment, as it can affect how budesonide is metabolized. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as difficulty breathing or loss of consciousness, call emergency services immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. Storage: Store budesonide at room temperature, away from heat and open flames, as it is flammable. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Additional Notes: This summary does not include all possible information about budesonide. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete details about this medication and your specific health needs.
